rows.title: Trump promised ‘rocket fuel.’ The economy got a ‘big yawn’ housing bill and higher debt than defense costs instead
rows.standfirst: Trump promised rate cuts; instead 10-year Treasury yields topped 4.7% and 30-year mortgage rates sit at 6.66%.

rows.title: Jensen Huang says ‘a lot’ of six-figure jobs in plumbing and construction will soon be unlocked because someone needs to build new AI centers
rows.standfirst: The AI boom is threatening white-collar, entry-level jobs—but the Nvidia CEO says it’s creating a six-figure opportunity for electricians and construction workers.

rows.title: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh talks a big game, but this market indicator will tell you if Wall Street trusts him after he caused a ‘credibility shock’
rows.standfirst: “The bottom line is that an important part of the Fed’s credibility is not just to say that it has certain goals but also to explain how it will achieve those goals.”

rows.title: The labor market could become so backward that the economy will have to shed jobs to keep unemployment steady
rows.standfirst: “Today, the labor market’s speed limit is much lower than just a few years ago, setting the stage for a jobless expansion.”

rows.title: He was homeless at 16. Now he sits on the board of David Beckham’s wellness company and his business is about to hit $1 billion in revenue
rows.standfirst: Hudson Leogrande, the founder of popular hoodie brand Comfrt, bounced between car sales and chimney telemarketing before hitting his stride as an entrepreneur.

rows.title: Two-thirds of parents say their adult Gen Z kids still rely on them financially for support—even though it’s putting them under strain
rows.standfirst: About 64% of parents say their adult Gen Z children still rely on them for money, housing, and more.

rows.title: Elon Musk wants engineers and trade talent: All you need is 3 bullet points, a résumé, and a desire to create the best data centers ‘off Earth’
rows.standfirst: Future work at SpaceX, the company has indicated, includes establishing a lunar economy, mining asteroids, and energy production on Mars.

rows.title: PwC U.S. CEO advises young workers to say yes a lot, even if it means working on the weekends—‘That person climbs into the next role’
rows.standfirst: PwC U.S. CEO Paul Griggs advises that “putting in time when people are not looking” is one of the best ways to climb the corporate totem pole.

rows.title: From Porsche penthouses to Nobu lofts: Inside the $67 billion boom in luxury branded residences
rows.standfirst: Inspired by the lifestyle-influencer ecosystem, luxury brands are turning condos into status symbols.

rows.title: Why a measly 100,000 job openings is normal for the Trump economy
rows.standfirst: June openings fell to 7.36 million, but immigration curbs and retirements may have pushed the break-even hiring rate close to zero.

rows.title: Kevin Warsh told Wall Street he’d be sharing less—Goldman Sachs fears a void of Fed facts will only amplify misinformation and instability
rows.standfirst: “Even without providing explicit forward guidance, central bankers still have an obligation to explain the economic framework behind their decisions. On that score, this press conference fell well short,” chimed professor Jeremy Siegel.

rows.title: Scott Bessent just declared the K-shaped economy is over, saying he’s ‘sick of hearing about’ it—but the data would beg to disagree
rows.standfirst: “I can say here definitively, the K-shaped economy is over.”

rows.title: Apollo CEO has a $11.1 billion net worth today—but he started out with a series of hospitality jobs, from valet parking to working in a party store
rows.standfirst: Just like other CEOs, Marc Rowan, the cofounder of Apollo Global Management, says “you have to take something away from” ordinary jobs.

rows.title: Locked out of housing, Gen Z and Millennials are building wealth in the stock market instead as they reach record high $3.1 trillion in holdings
rows.standfirst: Experts warn brokerage accounts lack a mortgage’s forced savings discipline and carry other risks

rows.title: Jamie Dimon waves off Wall Street ‘squealing like stuck pigs’ over Warsh’s Fed: ‘It makes tremendous sense’
rows.standfirst: “I wish them the best. They will, over time, do the right thing,” Dimon said.

rows.title: Over a third of employers handed out ‘peanut butter raises’ this year—now, a quarter of bosses admit they’re losing top talent because of bad pay
rows.standfirst: Around 36% of U.S. companies say they gave out across-the-board pay increases this year—and experts warn it’s killing motivation.

rows.title: For every 10 jobs, there are 2,539 applicants. A top hiring platform’s CEO has a solution to the job hunt hell: ‘Don’t just apply to OpenAI’
rows.standfirst: The job hunt hell is real—applications per recruiter are up 412%. But most applicants are chasing the same famous companies, says Greenhouse CEO Daniel Chait.

rows.title: The suit rule is dead. Researching your interviewer isn’t
rows.standfirst: You don’t have to wear a suit to your interview anymore. Unless, of course, you do.

rows.title: Bank of America is splashing out $250 million a year on weight loss drugs for its staff: ‘We see a great impact on employees,’ CEO says
rows.standfirst: Weight-loss drugs are becoming a popular perk, with almost a third of workers saying they’d even switch jobs for it. Bank of America has them covered.

rows.title: The deportation economy is backfiring on American workers, top economist warns
rows.standfirst: Diane Swonk says July’s bizarre jobs report is the first data from the deportation economy: shrinking payrolls and a shrinking workforce.

rows.title: CEO of the world’s largest workspace provider says commuting will be extinct by 2040—and your kids will think it’s ‘mad stuff’ professionals once did
rows.standfirst: CEO of IWG, Mark Dixon, says future generations will think it’s “mad stuff” that bosses once made workers “travel 100 miles to sit down and use a computer.”

rows.title: Meet the 33-year-old CEO betting on boomers chasing their grandkids—and millennials selling their first house
rows.standfirst: “Consumers are starved for better tools to help make one of the biggest financial decisions of their life,” says Kelley Blue Book Homes CEO John Liss.

rows.title: AI is changing work faster than the data can keep up
rows.standfirst: Recent studies have shown AI having a positive impact on job growth, yet economists and labor activists warn that the emerging technology threatens to quickly transform the financial system.

rows.title: The tables have turned: Florida and Texas are the biggest losers in the housing market as Ohio emerges a surprise winner
rows.standfirst: Cleveland is becoming one of the more desirable markets for homebuyers.

rows.title: This ‘hidden’ career path is in dire need of more workers—and it can pay Gen Z over $300,000 with no degree required
rows.standfirst: Six-figure salaries are within reach for Gen Z, but only if they’re willing to brave extreme weather, noisy tarmacs, and the smell of jet fumes.

rows.title: Teenagers are shooting out over 50 applications and getting ghosted even for volunteer jobs: ‘I’ll take anything at this point’
rows.standfirst: The summer job market has been “soul destroying” for teens in the U.S., Canada, and U.K.—but some are finding a way in.

rows.title: Corcoran Group CEO says Gen Z’s housing market struggles mirror what boomers faced 30 years ago: ‘Stop buying Starbucks coffee,’ she advises
rows.standfirst: From skipping coffee runs to hosting dinner clubs, Corcoran Group CEO Pamela Liebman has one message for Gen Z: Getting your first home takes sacrifices—but it’s doable, even in today’s pricey market.

rows.title: Mark Zuckerberg says the future will have an ‘abundance of jobs’—and predicts a wave of new careers like world builders and personal biologists
rows.standfirst: Despite predictions of a job apocalypse, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg sees a future of economic and financial prosperity.

rows.title: The stock market may be doing so well that it’s causing more baby boomers and Gen Xers to drop out of the labor force
rows.standfirst: “My hunch is that this is as at least partially attributable to wealth effects from record highs in the stock market.”

rows.title: Oil prices reverse gains in Strait of Hormuz standoff as Wall Street inches up ahead of inflation numbers
rows.standfirst: Futures ticked up for the S&P 500 as investors await Wednesday’s July inflation report, expected to ease slightly to 3.4% from 3.5%.

rows.title: The best time to start a business is in your 20s—not 30s—says cofounder of $2 billion toy giant Spin Master: ’No one sees you as competition’
rows.standfirst: While the average founder is 42 years old, Spin Master cofounder Ronnen Harary says your 20s is actually the best time to start a business.

rows.title: How a book that inspired Warren Buffett and a $14,000 side hustle helped billionaire Bill Ackman get started as an investor
rows.standfirst: Pershing Square Capital Management CEO Bill Ackman says he was inspired to become an investor after working at his dad’s real estate company.

rows.title: Mortgage rates hit one-year high at 6.69% as home sales fall
rows.standfirst: First-time buyers made up just 29% of July sales as inventory fell and mortgage rates priced out buyers, even as existing-home sales edged up.

rows.title: Meet ChatTJB, the ‘AI’ chatbot with no AI, no algorithm and no LLM. It’s just one guy and the 10,000 people who volunteered to type back
rows.standfirst: There’s no AI behind ChatTJB, just a former Google employee and soon, more than 10,000 volunteers answering strangers’ questions in his place.

rows.title: Google DeepMind’s chief AI exec started out detasseling corn in Indiana for around $1 an hour at 14: ‘I grew up in really humble beginnings’
rows.standfirst: Google DeepMind’s Lila Ibrahim had no AI pedigree—she started out with a $1 cornfield job, immigrant parents, and a habit of taking risks others missed.

rows.title: Wall Street futures rise ahead of inflation report as the Fed watches surging costs
rows.standfirst: Economists expect CPI to slow to 3.4% from June’s 3.5%, while strong quarterly results boosted Super Micro and other AI data-center suppliers

rows.title: Inflation came in perfectly on forecast. Almost everything underneath it is a ‘mess’ as wages struggle to keep up
rows.standfirst: July CPI offered some welcome relief, but the report masks stubborn rent increases and wages that can barely keep up.

rows.title: The majority of U.S. employers say they plan to increase hiring this year—these are the top roles they’re looking to fill
rows.standfirst: After years of job market hell, around two-thirds of U.S. employers are now planning to hire again—they’re looking for marketers, HR and tech workers.

rows.title: Wall Street tries to shake off a rough week as another inflation test looms
rows.standfirst: Futures rose ahead of Thursday’s producer price data, but Cisco’s 6% drop after strong earnings shows AI-stock nerves haven’t gone away.

rows.title: Trump’s ‘Golden Age’ economy pitch fizzles with midterm voters
rows.standfirst: Just 39% approve of Trump’s job performance and only 30% back his handling of inflation as Republicans grow anxious about affordability messaging

rows.title: Costliest U.S. bond sale since 2001 is investor warning to Bessent
rows.standfirst: Interest on the public debt continues to be a key driver of the budget deficit. For the fiscal year to date, the tally is $1.17 trillion — a 15% increase.

rows.title: ‘It’s not lights out for the economy’: U.S. retail sales drop 0.6% in July
rows.standfirst: There was a notable bump in spending in both April and May as Americans dipped into their tax refunds. That affect may have faded last month.

rows.title: Meet a 29-year-old influencer who calls herself a tradwife—but she’s really more of a homesteader
rows.standfirst: Traditional living is drawing younger consumers and becoming big business as creators turn old-fashioned skills into modern commerce.

rows.title: Trump’s grand plan to put American workers first may be backfiring as U.S.-born unemployment rises and wage growth stalls
rows.standfirst: “These jobs are typically ones that are very difficult, very arduous jobs that require a lot of physical hardship, and the native-born workers just haven’t done these jobs for quite some time and are in no mood to take them now—certainly not at these wages.”

rows.title: Exec at $27 billion tech giant HP hits back at Gen Z lazy label, saying they’re great at listening and building relationships
rows.standfirst: George Brasher says his Gen Z coworkers have a “healthy relationship with work” and know how to listen and build trust.

rows.title: ‘Godfather of AI’ says billionaires like Elon Musk are right about the future of work—but he predicts mass unemployment is on its way
rows.standfirst: While tech leaders paint a positive future where work is optional thanks to AI, the “Godfather of AI” Geoffrey Hinton warns they’re “betting on AI replacing a lot of workers.”

rows.title: Gen Z is eyeing up ‘secure’ healthcare jobs to AI-proof their careers, but be warned: Chiropractors, doctors and paramedics are the unhappiest workers
rows.standfirst: Health care workers report burnout and lower job satisfaction. In fact, Gen Z’s safest bet for happiness might just be behind a counter, not a stethoscope, research suggests.

rows.title: Billionaire founder agrees with Elon Musk, Sam Altman, and Jeff Bezos: We will live and work in space—and could be commuting to the moon by 2030
rows.standfirst: “We’ll have a moon base, people living and working on the moon,” says billionaire Voyager Technologies founder Dylan Taylor.

rows.title: Walmart, Target and Home Depot set to give Wall Street a peek at the American consumer, one week after stocks’ all-time high
rows.standfirst: Walmart, Target, Home Depot and Lowe’s report earnings this week after the steepest drop in U.S. retail spending in more than a year.

rows.title: A dropout living in a trailer, he got $1 million from Peter Thiel at 19—now he’s a billionaire who says the American Dream isn’t dead
rows.standfirst: Billionaire Palmer Luckey sold Oculus to Facebook for $2 billion by 21 years old—and says that kind of break “isn’t happening in China.”

rows.title: Home Depot rides America’s housing affordability problem to sales increase on home DIY projects
rows.standfirst: Revenue climbed to $47.86 billion and U.S. comparable sales rose 1.3%, but big-ticket renovations fell as high borrowing costs persist

rows.title: Top economist on Trump’s ‘deadly cocktail’ for the bond market—and how the bond vigilantes have crossed Scott Bessent’s ‘red line’
rows.standfirst: “The bond vigilantes have come out of hibernation,” Johns Hopkins’ Steve Hanke told Fortune, and “the inflation genie is out of the bottle.”

rows.title: Millionaire Mel Robbins says her waitressing boss taught her how to spot the most influential person in the room: ‘It’s never who you think it is’
rows.standfirst: “The Mel Robbins Podcast” host says the most powerful person in the room is “never who you think it is.”

rows.title: Ex-Google chief scientist tells Gen Z the trick is not to master AI—instead, just ‘skim papers’
rows.standfirst: Jeff Dean, who just left Google after 27 years, says future success belongs to Gen Z students who read broadly and focus on problems with a five-year horizon.

rows.title: Exclusive: A leader in Venezuela’s National Assembly engages ‘money doctor’ Steve Hanke for a dose of dollarization medicine in a nation sick from hyperinflation
rows.standfirst: The Johns Hopkins professor has spent five decades traveling the world, fighting for the cause of sound money. He’s taking on his biggest dragon yet.

rows.title: As U.S. debt hits $40 trillion, Americans will foot the bill: $700 a month for retirees, and homebuyers could take a $53,000 hit, report finds
rows.standfirst: “Addressing the national debt deserves to be a high priority for both voters and lawmakers, to benefit all Americans.”

rows.title: Moderna co-founder is a billionaire once again at $1.7 billion—he once turned down 20 high-paying job offers to ‘have more of an impact on the world’
rows.standfirst: Billionaire biotech pioneer Robert Langer advises workers to do what makes them happy over money and job security: “If you give up too easily, that’s not good.”

rows.title: Gen Z forced to rewrite the American Dream in the ‘Great Postponement’: Fixer-uppers, side hustles and doing life out of order
rows.standfirst: “We’ve not seen challenges in terms of affordability like this in more than a generation,” said Wharton professor Susan Wachter.

rows.title: Forget RTO: Fully remote workers report the highest well-being—and are less likely to quit, new study of 7,700 employees finds
rows.standfirst: The research found little evidence that remote workers felt less connected to colleagues or workplace culture—despite what CEOs like Jamie Dimon say.

rows.title: $25 billion CEO says one-hour interviews are a waste of time—he puts candidates through six hours of tests and wants them to order wine at lunch
rows.standfirst: Steve Jobs had his beer test. Bupa’s CEO has a six-hour interview process—and what drink you order at lunch tells him how confident you are.

rows.title: ‘We will not endure’ — Top Iranian leaders signal they are running out of time as economy crumbles ahead of Trump’s next sanctions onslaught
rows.standfirst: “As someone who has experienced war, we understand the true value of peace.”

rows.title: Even billionaires are worried their Gen Z kids can’t keep a job—and their wealth advisors say the fear is ‘very real’
rows.standfirst: It’s a “very real concern” for the ultrawealthy that their children aren’t prepared for the future, wealth advisor Tom Thiegs told Fortune.

rows.title: The CEO of $1.2 billion learning platform Preply says it all started with his online search for an English tutor
rows.standfirst: Kirill Bigai, the cofounder and CEO of learning platform Preply, had to take on a consulting gig while getting paid almost nothing building the business.

rows.title: How Washington’s interest bill on the $40 trillion national debt exploded 14% in 10-month budget period through July
rows.standfirst: The huge increase in interest expense has two sources.

rows.title: The Treasury doubled bond buybacks to bring down borrowing costs. The relief barely lasted
rows.standfirst: The 10-year Treasury yield is back near a one-year high as investors brace for fresh inflation data and the Fed’s Jackson Hole meeting.

rows.title: Goldman Sachs says America’s energy sector will need 500,000 more workers by 2030—and humanoid robots may have to step in
rows.standfirst: America’s energy sector is thriving thanks to AI. The only issue? There aren’t enough workers to meet the demand.

rows.title: Redfin ordered to reinstate listings, hire staff for the service under FTC settlement in Zillow case
rows.standfirst: Redfin agreed to shut down its internet listings and exclusively repost Zillow listings in exchange for $100 million and other compensation from Zillow, according to the FTC.

rows.title: Gen Z wants to be ‘tradwives.’ New data reveals the exact salary your spouse needs to earn—and in most states it’s under $100K
rows.standfirst: And for the average American family, one parent would need to be earning around $80,000 to sustain the other quitting their job to raise one child.

rows.title: Bill Gates fears world leaders are unprepared for 3 major AI risks: ‘Stunted’ child development, emboldened criminals, and vanishing jobs for Gen Z
rows.standfirst: “I believe we need time to prepare for the period of social, political, and economic upheaval we are about to enter.”

rows.title: Bill Gates wants to tax robots to deter businesses from replacing humans with machines
rows.standfirst: “The tax system nudges you toward replacing people with machines.”

rows.title: ‘I’m in favor of taxes,’ says Nvidia’s Jensen Huang—but he doesn’t agree with Bill Gates on his plan to slow an AI fallout
rows.standfirst: “I love the heck out of Bill … but I don’t see what he sees,” Huang said.

rows.title: After decades in the music industry, Pharrell Williams admits he never stops working: ‘If you do what you love everyday, you’ll get paid for free’
rows.standfirst: Grammy Award–winning artist Pharrell Williams says he’s always “being a student” and plans to “never stop working.” He advises others to follow their passion, not money.

rows.title: Kevin Warsh finally threw Wall Street some crumbs on what he’s thinking: ‘There is one signal nobody can miss: 65 months of elevated inflation’
rows.standfirst: But make no mistake: “We should not indulge a regime in which market participants are looking primarily to the Fed for their next trade.”

rows.title: ‘We have work to do’: Fed Reserve Chair Warsh suggests rate hike in coming months amid high inflation
rows.standfirst: Warsh says recent reports on inflation coming down does not tell him “underlying trends have meaningfully improved.”

rows.title: Why the Fed is often slow, late … and wrong in reading inflation
rows.standfirst: The central bank should pay more attention to the short-term trends that reveal an important “inflation regime change” may already be underway.

rows.title: New U.S. sanctions will hit ordinary Iranians hard. That may be the whole point as the crashing economy stirs fresh protests
rows.standfirst: “Digital assets and gold are how ordinary Iranians protect their savings from inflation.”

rows.title: The official jobless rate is so low the Fed thinks the economy is at full employment. But a gauge of the ‘functionally unemployed’ keeps climbing
rows.standfirst: “If this continues, it would suggest the labor market is losing strength despite what we may see in the headline unemployment numbers.”

rows.title: Women only accounted for 26% of hires in jobs with AI skills—and they could be missing out on a $100K salary difference
rows.standfirst: Women are up against a “triple penalty” when it comes to landing high-level lucrative AI roles, new LinkedIn data shows.

rows.title: The end of the driver’s license: Uber exec calls car ownership ‘the most inefficient asset’ and says no one will need one in 15 to 20 years
rows.standfirst: Uber president and COO Andrew Macdonald predicts that in two decades, most people will get around by bike, scooter, public transit, or autonomous vehicle.
